<reflection>
- The first experiment resulted in very similar negative log-likelihood (NLL) values for all 20 models, ranging tightly from -23.7 to -22.0. 
- This indicates that under standard, moderate conditions, the models possess enough parametric flexibility to fit the baseline kinetic curve almost equally well. 
- While the aim of establishing a baseline was achieved, the models remain highly degenerate. To break this degeneracy, we must perturb the system by moving away from standard conditions to selectively activate specific mechanistic features (like product binding or higher-order catalyst interactions).
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
By introducing a high initial product concentration (P=0.5), we can immediately distinguish models with product-induced deactivation or inhibition (M12, M17, M5) from the rest. These models will exhibit a suppressed initial rate or rapid early stalling compared to models that are insensitive to product. 
Simultaneously, increasing the catalyst concentration to 0.15 (a 3-fold increase from the first run) will disproportionately amplify second-order catalyst interactions (M2, M3, M13, M18, M19) by a factor of 9, making them easily distinguishable from first-order catalyst mechanisms. 
Decreasing the substrate concentration to 1.0 will reduce the relative impact of substrate-induced deactivation (M7, M11, M16), providing a clear contrast to the first experiment. This combination of high product, high catalyst, and lower substrate will pull apart the tightly clustered models by selectively activating product- and catalyst-dependent pathways while suppressing substrate-dependent ones.
</hypothesis>
